title: Methodology
content:
eMailCompare compares email providers by who runs them, where their servers are, what their terms and privacy policies say, and what you have to hand over to register. It does not recommend any provider.
Status of a provider Mark Meaning ✅ An account was registered and tested by hand 🤖 Data collected automatically (DNS, RDAP/WHOIS, the provider’s website); registration not tested yet ⏳ Pending: partial data, not reviewed yet ❌ The service is gone: shut down, under permanent maintenance or unreachable Comparison criteria Jurisdiction: country of the MX (mail) servers by GeoIP. For a domain without MX records, the country of its web server. Intelligence alliance: Five Eyes (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, New Zealand), Nine Eyes (adds Denmark, France, the Netherlands, Norway) and Fourteen Eyes (adds Germany, Belgium, Italy, Spain, Sweden), assigned from the jurisdiction. Domain created / expires: from RDAP or WHOIS. Domains registered in 2010 or earlier are green, domains from 2021 on are red. Registration requirements: whether signing up asks for an email to verify, a phone number or SMS code, or personal data such as name and address. Filled only after a manual test (✅). Terms of service and privacy policy: a short summary. Summaries of collected rows are keyword-based; follow the provider’s page for the full text. Infrastructure: A and MX records with the hosting network and its country. Colours Green: favourable — an old domain, no phone or personal data needed. Yellow: caution — optional data, Nine Eyes. Red: unfavourable — a very new domain, Five Eyes, required data. Purple: Fourteen Eyes. Grey: the service is gone. Data All data is public: DNS, RDAP/WHOIS, GeoIP and the providers’ own websites. It may be outdated or wrong. The source is emails.csv in the repository; this site is generated from it with Hugo. Corrections are welcome in Issues.

wölkli Mail - Secure and Encrypted Mail in Switzerland wölkli Mail is a Swiss service that provides secure and encrytped mail accounts hosted in Switzerland in its own ISO 27001 certified data centre.
Wölkli Mail is a Swiss email service offering free and paid encrypted email accounts under the @wail.ch domain. Hosting is provided in its own ISO 27001-certified data center in Switzerland. The service focuses on security and privacy, with a basic free tier (200 MB, no IMAP/SMTP) and paid plans with enhanced features. Security & Anonymity: Wölkli Mail employs 256-bit SSL encryption for data transmission and AES-256 server-side encryption for stored emails. It supports OpenPGP for message encryption and decryption, along with two-factor authentication (2FA). Emails are encrypted with user-specific cryptographic keys before reaching the inbox, preventing even the service provider from accessing their contents. Data is stored in Switzerland, benefiting from strict privacy laws (DSG). However, full anonymity isn’t guaranteed: registration requires a name, surname, and a strong password (min. 12 characters), and IP addresses may be logged. The privacy policy lacks detailed disclosure about data collection, leaving some uncertainty regarding anonymity. The free version (200 MB, 20 MB attachment limit, ad-free) is suitable for basic correspondence, temporary registrations, or non-sensitive data via the web interface (based on RainLoop, with Russian language support). Paid tiers, offering more storage and IMAP/SMTP access, are ideal for personal or professional use requiring encryption and reliability. Thanks to Swiss jurisdiction and cryptographic features, it’s a good fit for users prioritizing above-average privacy, though for maximum anonymity (e.g., no personal data required), alternatives like Proton Mail or Tutanota might be preferable.

title: xmail.net
content:
XMAIL.NET™ - Free Web Based Xmail
XMail is a free web-based email service that has been operational since 1998, accessible via xmail.net. Incorporated in the British Virgin Islands with IT operations subcontracted in Vancouver, Canada, XMail provides users with a simple and minimalist communication tool through an Ajax-powered browser interface. The service also offers 1 GB of mailbox storage and 1 GB for personal web hosting, making it a versatile option for basic internet tasks. Security & Anonymity: XMail stands out with its privacy policy: it collects no personal or demographic information during signup—users only need to choose a username and password. This ensures a high degree of anonymity, as no identity disclosure is required. The service is accessible via standard browsers, including Tor-compatible ones (e.g., Brave), adding optional anonymity when used through the Tor network. For secure communication, XMail supports S/MIME with personal certificates, enabling end-to-end encryption and digital signatures to verify sender authenticity. However, full data protection relies on utilizing these certificates, as server-side encryption isn’t specified. Inactive accounts are deleted after one year, preventing the accumulation of abandoned data. There’s no mention of data sharing with third parties, leaving legal obligations unclear (BVI jurisdiction). Use Cases: XMail is suitable for users who value basic anonymity and straightforward privacy without complexity. It’s a good fit for: Anonymous correspondence via the web interface or Tor (with S/MIME for encryption). Storing small amounts of data (1 GB for email and web files). Hosting simple static HTML web pages (no CGI/PHP support). Individuals avoiding intrusive data collection by larger services. It’s not suited for complex tasks requiring server-side scripting or highly sensitive communication without self-applied encryption. XMail is ideal for those seeking a lightweight, free, and anonymous tool for messaging and basic online presence, especially when paired with Tor for added protection. It’s a solution for everyday needs with a focus on simplicity and independence.
